introduce KV freelist defragmenter and selective hot-prefix pinning


Motivation: under high-concurrency, the paged KV cache freelist would fragment after repeated allocations/frees of mixed-size blocks, increasing allocation latency and causing more frequent slow-path compaction. This PR adds an opportunistic freelist defragmenter that compacts adjacent free pages on free-paths and a lightweight hot-prefix selective pinning policy so frequently-accessed key prefixes avoid costly eviction. Goals: reduce p99 allocation latency, lower background compaction pressure, and improve tail latency for workloads with hot prefixes (chat sessions, long contexts).

Summary of changes:
- Opportunistic freelist defragmenter run inline on frees when a small threshold of contiguous free segments is observed (configurable).
- Compact-on-free path that coalesces adjacent free pages into larger blocks to improve reuse for larger token sequences.
- Adaptive reuse scoring: tracks short-term reuse frequency per page bucket and prefers reuse of high-score pages.
- Hot-prefix selective pinning: a small resident pin set for top-N hot key prefixes with LRU eviction; pins are persisted across ephemeral reconnects to stabilize performance.

This PR introduces a weight prepack path and a small kernel-lane allocator that lets the runtime fuse smoothquant dequantization into the kernel dispatch without materializing intermediate dequant tensors. Goals: 1) lower wall-clock latency for first-token and steady-state by removing memory-bound dequant copies, 2) reduce peak GPU memory for multi-tenant workloads by prepacking int8 weights in a compact layout and sharing lane metadata across batches, 3) keep compatibility with existing KV cache and continuous-batching

citations.text:
introduce-session-decorator-to-simplify-cross-sdk-streams-and-credential-rotation


Context: Multiple SDKs exposed slightly different streaming iterator ergonomics and credential refresh hooks which made cross-language examples and platform integrations brittle. This PR introduces a lightweight SessionDecorator abstraction and a small set of shared semantics (ResumeToken v2 + telemetry markers) to harmonize behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go. Goal: make stream consumers simpler to implement, provide a single place for automatic credential rotation and graceful resume, and add telemetry points to measure reauth/backpressure heuristics.

Implementation notes:
- Python: session_decorator.py implements an async generator wrapper that catches AuthExpired errors, triggers the provided credential_provider.refresh() and retries from a resume_token. Adds small coordination via an async Lock so concurrent reauth attempts coalesce.
- TypeScript: sessionDecorator.ts implements an async iterable class that mirrors the Python contract, exports a withSessionDecorator factory that preserves stream typing.
- Go: session_decorator.go adds a StreamDecorator type with Resume(ctx, token) and Start(ctx) iterator model; uses channels to translate push->pull where necessary.

Motivation: the previous default (inject-first-returned) caused nondeterministic structured-output injection when multiple tools returned overlapping JSON fragments or produced idempotent but out-of-order updates. Design: add three merge strategies: first_wins (legacy), last_wins, and merge_patch (depth-aware JSON/struct merge that preserves keyed identities and deduplicates array items when an id key is present). Heterogeneous-bandwidth-aware allreduce fanout with KV-shard coalescing and comm/compute overlap


Motivation: on mixed-cluster deployments we observed long tail latency and suboptimal throughput for tensor-parallel allreduce when nodes have heterogeneous NVLink/intra-node bandwidths or asymmetric cross-node links. Smaller microbatches and low-latency applications (streaming chat) disproportionately hit these tails.

This PR introduces a bandwidth-aware fanout planner and a KV-shard coalescing pass that together reduce cross-node stalls and improve overlap between communication and compute. It also adds a narrow-copy optimized kernel for strided small-chunk merges and a runtime hook that maps comm streams to physical links based on a link-rate profile discovered at startup.

What changed (high level):
- Fanout planner: builds a minimal spanning fanout for allreduce that avoids slow links and increases per-hop concurrency when it detects bandwidth heterogeneity. The planner prefers intra-node NVLink-RDMA pairs, then high-rate cross-node links, and uses low-rate links only as fallback.
- KV-shard coalescer: groups adjacent KV cache shards into aligned coalesced writes to reduce the number of small allgathers. This reduces per-step launch overhead and amortizes DMA for common prefix cache hits.
- Stride-optimized memcpy kernel: a small, vectorized kernel for <4KB strided copies used by the coalescer; reduces memcpy time by up to 3x in microbenchmarks.
